Native combat report construction, DF 53.16 configured Windows PEs
================================================================

Source extraction: tools/extract_combat_announcement_sources.py.
The configured reference and classic images were read and disassembled locally.
Image identities: reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000; classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000.
This is static reconstructed source, not observed game output. The extractor
never executes the game, a translation, a generator, or a build. Addresses below
are reference native VAs; native-owners.tsv retains the independent classic VAs.
PE CHAININFO merges unwind pieces into complete logical native functions.
Each per-owner .asm retains every instruction, including non-text calculations;
native-control-flow.tsv retains conditions and branches; native-calls.tsv retains
direct calls/tail transfers; native-switches.tsv retains decoded case/default
paths; native-literals.tsv retains RIP strings, vector operands, inline stores.
Printable numeric immediates such as division constants gfff/VUUU and integer
argument 0x32 are source operands, not caption vocabulary. Text production below
is reconstructed by following string assign/append calls and string stores.

Complete typed dynamic input fields
----------------------------------
UNIT = complete native unit caption (0x14132e430), including player You, names,
       identities, complete creature/caste descriptions and complete professions.
OWNER = Your / UNIT + "'s" / native possessive pronoun your/his/her/its.
BODY = complete body-name formatter (0x1413345d0) or indicated inline RAW name.
LAYER = complete body/tissue/material field, optionally BODY + "'s " + TISSUE.
ITEM = complete native item caption (0x140c65450), preserving inner title,
       material, subtype, artwork subject and outer native quality/wear markers.
MATERIAL = complete native material/state name, optionally native creature owner.
Generated and authored identity/name fields are not finite English word lists.
The screenshot's +larch figurine of blood gnats+ is one ITEM with quality markers,
wood material and figure subject, not an English word substituted in isolation.

Attack-record producer 0x14064a350..0x1406536b2
----------------------------------------------
Normal item attack obtains attack definitions from virtual item+0x438.
An attack definition stores base verb at +0x10, third-person verb at +0x30 and
weapon subpart at +0x50. The native producer copies those complete string fields
at 0x14064ae64..0x14064ae9b. Adventure player selects base, all other actors select
third-person at 0x14064af2d..0x14064af54. Missing/invalid item attack definition
selects literal strike/strikes (0x14064af07..0x14064af28). Projectile setup initially
assigns strikes (0x14064a9e6). A special shove uses push/pushes (0x14064b97a).
Creature attack paths obtain the corresponding complete RAW ATTACK_VERB fields.
The stealth branch prefixes "silently " to the already selected attack verb
(0x140650ebe..0x140650ef5); it does not alter the actor's identity.

INSTRUMENT = ["the " + complete SUBPART + " of "] + POSSESSIVE + " " + ITEM,
             or POSSESSIVE + " " + complete anatomical instrument BODY.
SUBPART is omitted when empty or equal to NO_SUB (0x14064af6a..0x14064af8f).
For a present subpart, 0x14064af91..0x14064afc5 appends the/of wrapper; it does
not constrain subpart to shaft, pommel or flat. PLAYER POSSESSIVE is your;
other actors use native sex-based possessive pronoun (0x14064afdc..0x14064b034).
ITEM is appended whole at 0x14064b063 with caption detail argument false.
The body instrument alternative at 0x14064b736..0x14064b7b3 uses the same ownership.

ACTOR = UNIT for a creature actor; with projectile:
        "The flying " + ITEM / "The spinning " + ITEM / "The " + ITEM.
Projectile material/state/type/flags select motion, independently of ITEM.
See 0x14064a82a..0x14064a8eb and shared-damage 0x1400e5887..0x1400e5951.

Every finite direct sentence family of this producer:
  UNIT + " has moved out of range!"                 0x14064a578
  UNIT + (" let" | " lets") + " the " + BODY +
      " drop away as " + UNIT + (" attack." | " attacks.")
                                                   0x14064bb11..0x14064bbed
  UNIT + (" catch " | " catches ") + OWNED_BODY +
      " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"                 0x14064bfe9..0x14064c33c
  ACTOR + (" attack " | " attacks ") + UNIT + " but " + EVASION + "!"
                                                   0x14064d2f8..0x14064d7c5,
                                                   0x14064e2ba..0x14064e3b1
  EVASION = UNIT + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" |
                    " jump" | " jumps") + " away"
  UNIT + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" |
          " jump" | " jumps") + " away from " + ACTOR + "!"
                                                   0x14064e08a..0x14064e112
  ACTOR + (" miss " | " misses ") + UNIT + "!"  0x14064e61b..0x14064e658
  ACTOR + (" miss " | " misses ") + UNIT +
      " badly, blocked by the divine intervention of mighty " + DEITY + "!"
                                                   0x140650242..0x1406502c4
  SHOT + " but the shot is blocked!"              0x14064d55c
  SHOT + " but the shot is blocked" + [" with " + ITEM] + "!"
                                                   0x14064f1e4..0x14064f254
  SHOT + " but the shot is " + [PARRY_ADVERB] + "parried" +
      [" by " + ITEM] + "!"                      0x14064db47..0x14064dc18
  SHOT + " but the shot is " + [DEFLECT_ADVERB] + "deflected" +
      [" by " + ITEM] + "!"                      0x14064f933..0x14064fa0c
  SHOT = ACTOR + (" strike at " | " strikes at ") + UNIT
  PARRY_ADVERB = "deftly " | "just barely " | "easily " | empty
  DEFLECT_ADVERB = "effortlessly " | "narrowly " | "easily " | empty
  UNIT + (" block " | " blocks ") + ACTOR + [" with " + ITEM] + "!"
                                                   0x14064f299..0x14064f325
  UNIT + (" bat " | " bats ") + ACTOR + (" aside" | " out of the air") +
      [" with " + ITEM] + "!"                    0x14064fa4c..0x14064faf9
  UNIT_LIST + (" are " | " is ") + "stunned by divine power!"
                                                   0x140650b9e..0x140650c9a
  "Many are stunned by divine power!"             0x140650b5d..0x140650c9a
  UNIT_LIST preserves every selected unit with comma, comma-and, or and joining.
  UNIT + (" have" | " has") + " become enraged!" 0x14065336e..0x14065340f

The weapon optional clauses are omitted on null item pointer paths. Actor,
defender, projectile and equipment retain distinct typed ownership.
No adverb branch is a generalized global word replacement.

Additional complete prefixes passed through shared damage (record flag0x20):
  "The force bends the " + BODY                  0x1406530ad
  "The force twists the " + BODY                 0x1406530d8
  "The force pulls the " + BODY                  0x140653106
The three prefixes are stored in the damage record at 0x14065317d..0x1406531b1
and submitted to shared damage at 0x1406531ef, preserving every suffix family.

Wrestling producer 0x140646f00..0x14064a348
----------------------------------------
Subject inflection selects base for the adventure player and third-person for
other units. OWNED_BODY always contains owner plus the complete anatomical part.
Finite direct productions, with their original punctuation:
  UNIT + (" lock " | " locks ") + OWNED_BODY + " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"
                                                   0x140647499..0x140647576
  UNIT + (" place" | " places") + " a chokehold on " + OWNED_BODY +
      " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"               0x140647671..0x140647733
  UNIT + (" take " | " takes ") + UNIT + " down by the " + BODY +
      " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"               0x140647850..0x140647912
  UNIT + (" throw " | " throws ") + UNIT + " by the " + BODY +
      " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"               0x1406479f1..0x140647ab3
  UNIT + (" adjust" | " adjusts") + " the grip of " + OWNED_BODY +
      " on " + OWNED_BODY + "."                0x14064828d..0x14064834f
  UNIT + (" struggle" | " struggles") + " in vain against the grip of " +
      OWNED_BODY + " on " + OWNED_BODY + "."    0x1406486d2..0x140648794
  UNIT + (" release" | " releases" | " loosen" | " loosens") +
      (" the choke hold of " | " the joint lock of ") + OWNED_BODY +
      " on " + OWNED_BODY + "."                0x140648861..0x140648bde
  UNIT + (" release" | " releases" | " break" | " breaks") +
      " the grip of " + OWNED_BODY + " on " + OWNED_BODY + "."
                                                   0x140648ca5..0x140648e04,
                                                   0x1406494fe..0x140649601
  "The " + BODY + " is ripped away and remains in " + OWNER +
      (" mouth!" | " grip!")                    0x140649254..0x1406492e0
  UNIT + (" lose" | " loses") + " hold of the " + BODY + "!"
                                                   0x1406493b9..0x140649409
  UNIT + (" pass" | " passes") + " out."       0x140649a0d..0x140649a37
  UNIT + (" miss " | " misses ") + UNIT + "!"  0x140649ea3..0x140649ed2
Release/loosen branches choose either ownership order from native hold records;
the full owned fields must be carried in the selected order.

Prefixes forwarded into every shared-damage outcome:
  UNIT + (" pinch " | " pinches ") + OWNED_BODY + " with " + OWNED_BODY
                                                   0x140647d60..0x140647e2e
  UNIT + (" gouge " | " gouges ") + OWNED_BODY + " with " + OWNED_BODY
                                                   0x140647fe8..0x1406480b6
  UNIT + (" bend " | " bends ") + OWNED_BODY + " with " + OWNED_BODY
                                                   0x140648491..0x14064855e
  UNIT + (" shake " | " shakes ") + UNIT + " around by the " + BODY
                                                   0x14064903d..0x1406490a0
  UNIT + (" strangle " | " strangles ") + OWNED_BODY
                                                   0x1406497b7..0x140649866
The separate grab/grabs branch 0x140649ccf..0x140649d41 populates the ordinary
attack-record verb/instrument and uses the same normal damage-head constructor.

Grip state producer 0x141361370..0x141362544
------------------------------------------
Two complete owner/body pairs are constructed from units/body records; empty
singular RAW vectors or invalid body index use body part, and the plural path
uses body parts. Player ownership is Your, otherwise complete UNIT + "'s".
Success and positive grip record+0x1e:
  UNIT + (" release" | " releases") + " the grip of " + OWNED_BODY_A +
      " from " + OWNED_BODY_B + "."             0x141361ed8..0x141361fb1
Success and nonpositive record+0x1e:
  UNIT + (" break" | " breaks") + " the grip of " + OWNED_BODY_B +
      " from " + OWNED_BODY_A + "!"             0x141361fd3..0x1413620ac
Failure (input success byte false at 0x141361e8e):
  UNIT + (" are unable to break" | " is unable to break") + " the grip of " +
      OWNED_BODY_B + " on " + OWNED_BODY_A + "!" 0x14136210e..0x1413621f7
The from/on relation and swapped owner order are distinct source branches.

Embedded item producer 0x140643f70..0x140646e24
--------------------------------------------
  UNIT + (" pull" | " pulls") + " on the embedded " + ITEM + "."
                                                   0x140645253..0x14064543a
  UNIT + (" try" | " tries") + " to remove " + ITEM + "."
                                                   0x14064560f..0x1406457f8
Caption arguments false/-1 at 0x1406452a0 and the corresponding remove branch.
Terminal periods are inline stores 0x1406452e2 and 0x14064569d, not C strings.
Item-removal job 0x141397100..0x141397497:
  UNIT + " pulls out and " + ("drops" | "releases") + " " + ITEM + "."
                                                   0x141397273..0x141397332
Native item predicate 0x1413610f0 chooses drops/releases; the job does not choose
a base-person alternative, even though UNIT may itself be the player caption.

Charge producer 0x140654d20..0x140657a56
-------------------------------------
  UNIT + (" leap at " | " leaps at " | " charge at " | " charges at ") +
      UNIT + [" from behind" | " from the side"] + "!"
                                                   0x140655915..0x1406559d3
  UNIT + (" are " | " looks ") + "surprised by the ferocity of " +
      OWNER + " onslaught!"                     0x140655ab6..0x140655b5d
  UNIT + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" |
          " jump" | " jumps") + " away!"       0x14065622a..0x14065643e
  UNIT + (" collide" | " collides") + " with " + UNIT + "!"
                                                   0x140656634..0x140656733
  UNIT + (" are" | " is") + " knocked over!"   0x140656d1a..0x14065719c
  UNIT + (" are" | " is") + " knocked over" +
      (" and tumble" | " and tumbles") + " backward!"
                                                   0x140656a24..0x140656b6d,
                                                   0x140656ef6..0x14065703d
  UNIT + (" bounce" | " bounces") + " backward!" 0x140657215..0x140657497
  "You tangle together and tumble forward!" | "They tangle together and tumble forward!"
                                                   0x140657532..0x140657597
  "You tangle together and fall over!" | "They tangle together and fall over!"
                                                   0x1406576f8..0x14065779b

Collision/projectile movement and impact producers
-------------------------------------------------
Collision 0x140eadea0..0x140eb3ac4:
  UNIT + (" skip" | " skips") + " across the " +
      ("water" | "magma" | "lava") + "!"      0x140eae9d7..0x140eaea96
  UNIT + (" slam" | " slams") + " into an obstacle!"
                                                   0x140eaf64e..0x140eaf67c,
                                                   0x140eb38a9..0x140eb38d6
  UNIT + (" slam" | " slams") + " into an obstacle and " +
      ("blow" | "blows") + " apart!"           0x140eaf3e1..0x140eaf46e,
                                                   0x140eb368b..0x140eb3711
  UNIT + (" slam" | " slams") + " into " + UNIT + "!"
                                                   0x140eb0235..0x140eb02e5,
                                                   0x140eb1c83..0x140eb1d2e,
                                                   0x140eb2f8a..0x140eb3044
  UNIT + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" |
          " jump" | " jumps") + " out of " + OWNER + " flight path!"
                                                   0x140eb1167..0x140eb12d6
Projectile movement 0x140ea8fb0..0x140eade98:
  UNIT + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" |
          " jump" | " jumps") + " away from the " + ITEM + "!"
                                                   0x140eab966..0x140eabb6e
Projectile motion invokes normal attack producer at 0x140eaab49, 0x140eac4b6,
0x140ead66b, 0x140ead79b and 0x140eadb1b. Collision similarly invokes it at
0x140eafda0 and 0x140eb0760, and invokes bodily impact for obstacle damage.

Bodily impact 0x1413b1580..0x1413b209d, positive force only:
  PREFIX = OWNER + " " + INLINE_BODY + " takes the full force of the impact"
                                                   0x1413b1b72
Ground skid 0x1413b20a0..0x1413b2a26, positive force only:
  PREFIX = OWNER + " " + INLINE_BODY + " skids along the ground"
                                                   0x1413b25b8
INLINE_BODY = singular RAW name for count<=1, plural RAW name for count>1,
body part for invalid body index, or body part/body parts for absent RAW names.
The native verbs remain takes/skids even when the selected RAW name is plural.
Both producers copy the COMPLETE prefix to record.kind0x12 with flag0x20, then
invoke shared damage: 0x1413b1cdc and 0x1413b2725. Thus skidding is a separate
prefix family composing with all damage suffixes, not a standalone status word.

Fire, web and material emission
------------------------------
0x1413650e0..0x1413654b6 breath defense:
  UNIT + (" block" | " blocks") +
      (" the fire." | " the dragonfire." | " the breath.")
enum input 0=fire, 1=dragonfire, 2=breath at 0x1413652ff..0x14136533f;
out-of-range enum submits only UNIT + block/blocks, with no object/punctuation.
0x1413654c0..0x141365983 and 0x141366000..0x1413664c6:
  UNIT + (" breathe" | " breathes") + " fire!"
0x141365990..0x141365ffa:
  UNIT + (" hurl" | " hurls") + " a ball of fire!"
0x1413664d0..0x141366854:
  UNIT + (" shoot" | " shoots") + " out thick strands of webbing!"
0x1413c72b0, 0x1413c8f60, 0x1413c9ad0, 0x1413ca1d0:
  UNIT + (" breathe" | " breathes") + " a cloud of " + MATERIAL + "!"
0x1413c80b0:
  UNIT + (" breathe" | " breathes") + " a glob of " + MATERIAL + "!"
Cloud/glob material can be builtin, plant, creature-owned or historical-creature
material; failed material resolution uses literal unknown material. The vapor
state appends " vapor". Native owner + "'s " and complete material name stay one
typed MATERIAL phrase. Source operands include these alternatives, not just fire.

Material ownership has three distinct native constructions:
  MATERIAL = complete RAW material/state name, with any complete material prefix;
  MATERIAL = (complete RAW species name | historical/assumed identity name) +
             "'s " + complete RAW material/state name;
  MATERIAL = "'s " + complete RAW material/state name, when the selected native
             identity has no name. This last construction is an actual source
             branch, not an empty translated capture or a guessed owner.
An absent material lookup may substitute unknown material in those same fields;
the vapor-state branch appends " vapor" after the full owned or owner-free field.

The empty-identity branch follows the native string construction directly:
0x1413c7525..0x1413c753d initializes the temporary name to an empty string;
0x1413c7541..0x1413c7579 selects assumed identity or the historical figure name.
At 0x1413c7582, name.has_name(+0x72)==false jumps to 0x1413c75a2 and skips the
name formatter. 0x1413c75a2..0x1413c75b6 nevertheless appends the still-empty
temporary string. 0x1413c75c1..0x1413c75cc then unconditionally appends "'s ".
Thus the owner bytes are exactly "'s ", and the subsequently appended complete
material produces actual "'s blood", "'s unknown material" or another RAW name.
Repeated identity blocks around 0x1413c7798 and 0x1413c79b8 have the same has_name
guard and unconditional apostrophe-s append. The glob producer repeats this at
0x1413c841c/0x1413c859e; the alternate cloud producer repeats it at 0x1413c923f,
0x1413c943c and 0x1413c965c. A real empty name must not be assigned an invented
species/identity or silently discarded during translation.

Vapor fallback append sequence is explicit: 0x1413c7886 selects "unknown material",
0x1413c7893..0x1413c7897 appends the selected material, and 0x1413c78a2 selects
" vapor" for the final append. The equivalent alternate cloud sites are
0x1413c94fb (unknown material) and 0x1413c9517 (vapor). Consequently the finite
fallbacks include "unknown material vapor" and "'s unknown material vapor",
as well as a named owner plus the complete material-vapor phrase.

Complete item caption with combat arguments
------------------------------------------
Logical owner 0x140c65450..0x140c65f0a; classic 0x140c62490..0x140c62f4a.
Combat instrument, projectile, object, blocking item, embedded item and removed
item call this function with detail argument r8b=false; count is -1 or 1.

if false && artifact reference exists && artifact.name_present(+0x7a):
    return language_name(artifact+0x8);  // 0x140c654b9..0x140c654e2
    // The result is a BARE generated artifact name, with no material/type.
if false && item_type==0x59 && nonempty item title(+0xe8):
    return complete_title + " (copy)"; // 0x140c654fc..0x140c65513
if false && item_type==0x56 && written content/improvement has nonempty title:
    return complete_written_title + " (copy)";
    // 0x140c65521..0x140c656f4; improvement kinds0xc/0x9; failed/empty lookup
    // falls through to ordinary subtype caption, rather than inventing a title.
ordinary:
    construct virtual article-title(+0x5f0, count), quality/improvement markers,
    wear wrappers, native ownership/magic marks and virtual full title(+0x5e8).
    // All 98 item owner methods and type/material/RAW suppliers are preserved
    // by data/extracted/item-description-sources.tsv. Specialized book, cage,
    // slab, statue/figurine, food, corpse and tool captions enter those methods.
    // Custom named cages/designations are authored fields, not adjective lists.
    // Artifact-name and written-title early returns bypass the ordinary title.
Quality/wear wrappers are whole item decorations, not ownership delimiters.
The finite dispatch branches are unchanged when an arbitrary item is wielded as
an improvised weapon; translating only material/type nouns omits bare names.

Shared damage and companion state/death source ownership
-------------------------------------------------------
0x1400e56a0..0x1400e9f40 is re-extracted here in reference-e56a0.asm and classic.
Its fully reconstructed production tree is recorded in
data/extracted/announcement-combat-status/decompiled-shared-damage.txt and
decompiled-productions.tsv: ordinary/prebuilt heads; flag0x4 by-the vs in-the;
flag0x8 item vs body; direction behind/side; optional complete instrument;
deflection, tapping, no-force, pass-through, glance-away, all destroyed-layer
outcomes, detached-part/torso outcomes, every damage verb and omitted-repeat-verb
list, hole/jamming/fraction/equipment/fluid suffix, artery/nerve/ligament/tendon
injury flag ordering, gelding, equipment break, interruption, rage, embedded
item, latching, propulsion, unconsciousness, repeated stun/breathing/sickness,
injected/poured/flowed/splattered/crumbled/sucked material and silent record cases.
These source records are shared by ordinary strikes, wrestling, collision,
full-impact, force bend/twist/pull and the newly identified ground-skid head.
0x1400e9ecc is the 29-case aux dispatch; three preceding six-case injury tables
and unsigned-default branches are preserved in native-switches.tsv.
Null item lookup can leave the relation or deflection connector with no object;
optional item/prefix/body fields must retain that branch's ownership and spelling.

Companion status and death producers are separately extracted from both PEs in
data/extracted/announcement-status and data/extracted/fortress-missing-death.
Their status-update, state-helper, full unit/role/name suppliers and direct
submission paths include vomiting, recovery, pain/unconsciousness, hunger/thirst,
exposure, agitation/mood and death announcements that coexist with battle reports.
These finite native captions enter the existing announcement state grammar.

Installed RAW attack inputs
---------------------------
raw-attack-fields.tsv retains every ATTACK and ATTACK_VERB source token in both
configured games' vanilla and installed_mods object directories and available
mods object directories. raw-procedural-attack-sources.tsv retains every matching
installed vanilla Lua source expression; literal fields join the verb/part tables.
raw-source-roots.tsv records those source ownership classes: a file in mods is
an available candidate, not proof that it was loaded into the running world.
Current finite weapon subparts: flat, handle, helve, pommel, shaft. NO_SUB omits
the subpart construction entirely and is not displayed. Complete RAW verbs retain
both base and third-person forms in raw-attack-verbs.tsv. Additional jab/jabs come
from available Steam MOD 2925028826 (500502), item_extra_weapons.txt:152,164.
Unknown future RAW verbs/parts are dynamically supplied strings; spelling alone
does not provide translation or an identity-source classification.
